thread:
mike: Quick sync — thinking about making autoscale + SLA fallback composed of small policy modules instead of one big monolith. Operator executes admission and fast fallbacks; control plane composes tenant policy graphs and pushes them. :thinking:

sana: I like the split. Operator owning the fast path (evict/throttle/model-swap) makes sense for reliability. Control plane can coordinate higher-level decisions. :+1:

raj: main worry: if operator handles fallback decisions locally we might lose cross-tenant visibility for cost-driven fallbacks. How do we avoid cost surprises?

olivia: idea: operator exposes a tiny hook API so control plane can annotate requests with a policy hash and soft budget hints. Operator still enforces local safety. Example policy bundle (pseudo-YAML):
```yaml
policies:
  - name: latency_slo
    type: slo
    args: {p99_ms: 200}
  - name: budget_guard
    type: cost
    args: {daily_tokens: 1e6}
  - name: degrade_sequence
    type: fallback
    args: {variants: [quantized, smaller-model, throttle]}
```

mike: Nice. So control plane builds the bundles (and can change them during rollouts) and operator keeps a cached runtime config keyed by bundle hash. If cp unreachable, operator falls back to "degenerate" bundle baked into the operator image.

sana: +1 for baked degenerate defaults. Also: operator should accept two levels of directives — hard (must obey, e.g., tenant blackout) and soft (recommendation, e.g., cost hints).

raj: For cost-driven decisions we probably need periodic reconciliation reports back to control plane so we can adjust budgets. Otherwise ops teams get surprised by throttles.

olivia: Agreed — operator -> cp heartbeat with counters (tokens consumed, fallbacks triggered). Keep the channel narrow to avoid perf impact.

mike: How about canary rollouts of policy bundles? Control plane can mark a bundle as canary and tag a small percent of traffic. Operator enforces but also reports detailed traces for canary tenants only.

raj: Edge case: network partition between cp and operator. Operator should be conservative: prefer degrading model quality over returning errors. -> degrade sequence: quantized -> smaller-model -> throttle.

olivia: Pseudocode for operator runtime decision: 
```
decision = evaluate_local_hard_rules(req)
if decision == allow:
  decision = evaluate_bundle(req, bundle_hash)
if cp_unreachable:
  decision = apply_degnerate_bundle(req)
emit_metrics(decision)
return decision
```

mike: Typo: "degnerate" -> "degenerate" :D

deploy-bot: deploy: operator-image:v2026-03-18 pushed to staging (sha:abc123)

sana: Nice, that gives us a testbed. Proposal for immediate next steps: 1) short RFC describing operator contract + degenerate bundle, 2) implement bundle hash caching and heartbeat metrics, 3) add canary tagging in control plane.

mike: I'll draft the RFC today and ping you all. @sana can you own operator contract PR? @raj own cost/budget telemetry, @olivia write canary test plans. I'll schedule a 30m sync if needed. :calendar:

olivia: happy to write tests. one ask: include an explicit opt-out so tenants can disable model-degrade if they prefer hard fail. (enterprise customers will want that)

sana: add that as a hard-flag in bundle metadata: allow_degrade: false/true. ok to make default = true.

raj: I'll sketch metrics fields we need and an alert threshold draft.

mike: Great — thanks everyone. I'll post RFC link here when ready. :rocket:
